input.story: I deliver food for an app in Jaipur. They deactivated my ID last week and are holding 8,500 of my earnings for the last 2 weeks. Support just sends automated replies. Am I an employee? Can I claim salary?

output.masked_story: I deliver food for an app in Jaipur. They deactivated my ID last week and are holding 8,500 of my earnings for the last 2 weeks. Support just sends automated replies. Am I an employee? Can I claim salary?

case.problem_subtype: delivery app withheld earnings after ID deactivation
case.summary: The user works as a food delivery executive for an app in Jaipur. Their ID was deactivated last week and the platform is withholding 8,500 rupees of their earnings for the last two weeks with only automated responses from support.
case.user_goal: Retrieve unpaid earnings and understand employment/payment rights
evidence_missing: delivery app agreement or terms of service
payment history or bank statements showing previous payouts
screenshots of earnings dashboard showing the withheld amount
follow_up_questions: Do you have screenshots of your earnings dashboard showing the 8,500 rupees balance?
Did you receive any official email or message explaining why your ID was deactivated?
Do you have a copy of the contract or terms of service you agreed to when joining the delivery app?

lines: Other dues (leave encashment, reimbursements, etc.): Rs 8,500
notes: Check your offer letter/payslips for the exact gross vs in-hand salary. Gratuity, if any, has separate rules - ask a lawyer.
Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: As a delivery executive, your withheld earnings of 8,500 rupees are protected under wage rules, requiring final dues to be paid promptly . Your position is strong regarding the delivery of work, but your main weakness is the lack of written proof or a formal agreement currently in hand. The platform must justify any deductions or withheld amounts, as unauthorized deductions are prohibited [KB:src_cow_2019_18]. You have up to 3 years to file a formal claim for unpaid wages before the designated labour authority [KB:cow_s45].

options.title: Send a written message or email to support
options.what_to_do: Request a clear explanation for the ID deactivation and demand immediate release of your 8,500 rupees earnings.

options.title: Approach the Labour Department
options.what_to_do: File a formal application for unpaid wages before the authority appointed under the Code on Wages [KB:cow_s17] if the platform fails to respond.

options.title: Seek free legal aid
options.what_to_do: Contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for guidance if the platform continues to ignore your claims.

proof_tips: Take clear screenshots of your earnings dashboard showing the 8,500 rupees balance before your access is completely blocked.
Save any automated messages or emails received from the delivery app regarding your ID deactivation.
Gather bank statements showing past payments received from the platform to prove your working relationship.
what_i_dont_know: The exact terms of service or independent contractor agreement you signed with the delivery platform.
Whether the platform claims any specific policy violation or operational damage that led to the deactivation and withholding of funds.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: You can start by contacting support and filing a complaint with the labour authority yourself. A lawyer is not needed at this initial stage unless the platform initiates legal proceedings against you.
assessment.reply: Your position is clear: the delivery platform has withheld 8,500 rupees of your earnings after deactivating your ID, and you have the right to demand your final dues . Since you currently only receive automated responses, your best first step is to gather screenshots of your earnings dashboard and send a formal written demand via email or in-app support. If they do not release your money, you can file a claim before the labour authority within 3 years [KB:cow_s45].
